transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rohan Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Elena Martinez (BlueHarbor CISO), David Park (Head of Infra), Priya Singh (Security Engineer), Carlos Ruiz (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick posture review focused on SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 alignment, Trust Center access, RBAC/SSO, audit logging retention and format, encryption/KMS options, and data residency controls. Agreed to share reports and a controls mapping spreadsheet; follow-up demo of Trust Center and audit log walkthrough.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll give it a few seconds for folks to pop in. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. With me are Rohan and Liam from our security and infra team.
[00:10] Elena Martinez: thanks Maya. I'm Elena, CISO at BlueHarbor. We have David, Priya and Carlos on too. We got some questions about SOC 2, ISO mapping and how you expose audit logs.
[00:20] Maya: great, high level agenda  SOC 2/ISO posture, trust center access, RBAC/SSO, logs and encryption, and any procurement questions at the end. Sound good?
[00:25] David Park: yes, please. We're on a tight timeline to close compliance gaps before our Q4 audit, so specifics help.
[00:30] Rohan Patel: quick context from Redwood  we have a SOC 2 Type II report covering our hosted service, and we've published an ISO 27001 scope overview. We also provide a Trust Center with artifacts, and we can do dedicated VPC/private deployments for customers needing stronger isolation.
[00:45] Elena: is the SOC 2 report full coverage for hosted API and Dedicated, or only hosted?
[00:50] Rohan: the Type II covers our hosted API and control environment for the core control plane; Dedicated/reserved capacity environments are included for the managed offering when contracted. For on-prem or self-managed stacks we provide a controls guidance package but those environments sit outside our attestations. (slight pause) sorry, that was a mouthful.
[01:05] Priya Singh: when you say "controls guidance package"  does that include a mapping to ISO 27001 clauses and evidence we can reuse?
[01:10] Liam O'Neill: yep, we maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet that cross-references SOC 2 controls to ISO 27001 Annex A clauses and includes typical evidence artifacts and where they live in Trust Center. We'll share that after the call.
[01:20] Elena: perfect. For BlueHarbor we need to demonstrate control coverage for data residency and encryption. What's your default data residency policy?
[01:28] Rohan: hosted customers can select region on provisioning  we offer regions in NA, EU, APAC. For data residency guarantees we rely on contractual terms in our DPA and can pin model and storage to a specific region; for Dedicated we run in the region you choose, obviously. Note: backups and some control plane metadata may be replicated for availability  that's documented in the DPA.
[01:45] David Park: how do you handle audit logs? We need record-level, retention 3 years, and logs shipped to our Splunk / S3.
[01:52] Rohan: we emit tenant-scoped audit logs for authentication events, API calls (route, model, tokens consumed), config changes, and admin actions. Logs can be exported via syslog/S3 push or streamed to our partner integrations. Retention defaults to 90 days in the hosted plan but can be extended with add-ons or by choosing Dedicated with custom retention. For three years, we'd recommend the audit retention add-on or a VPC deployment with S3 bucket retention policy on your side.
[02:15] Priya: is the audit log schema stable? We need timestamps in ISO 8601, user IDs, action type, request payload hashes  can you confirm fields?
[02:22] Rohan: yes ISO 8601 timestamps, actor (user/service principal), action type, resource, request_id, status code, and an optional content_hash field for payload. We'll send sample logs. There have been minor field name variations historically (we recently changed resource->resource_id), I'll note that in the sample.
[02:40] Elena: what about RBAC and SSO integration? We use Okta and need SCIM provisioning, SAML SSO, and role-based access controls that map to our internal roles.
[02:48] Liam: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user provisioning. RBAC is customizable  we have a set of built-in roles (Admin, Developer, ReadOnly, Auditor) and you can create custom roles with specific permissions. For delegated admin and separation-of-duties you can create groups via SCIM and map. We'll send our role matrix.
[03:05] David Park: any support for attribute-based access or just group mapping?
[03:08] Rohan: primarily group and role mapping today; attribute-based policies are on the roadmap. We can support custom claims for session attributes in SAML to assist with mapping.
[03:18] Elena: encryption  at rest and in transit, customer-managed keys?
[03:22] Rohan: in transit: TLS 1.2+; at rest: platform-managed encryption by default with AES-256. For enterprise customers we offer CMEK via major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault)  this is available for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers can request CMEK for an additional compliance add-on.
[03:40] Priya: are keys ever held by Redwood? That is, do you have access to plaintext if CMEK is enabled?
[03:46] Liam: with CMEK Redwood does not have the raw key material; we call your KMS for decryption operations. However some metadata and caching KVs for inference sessions are handled in memory on our hosts; we can document the memory handling. For highest assurance, Private on-prem deployment keeps keys entirely under your control.
[04:05] Carlos Ruiz: from procurement perspective we need to understand what's in the DPA and what SLAs are available for Dedicated. Also pricing for the audit-log retention add-on.
[04:12] Maya: we will share the standard DPA and SLA tiers. Pricing for longer retention is tiered by retention length and ingestion volume; I'll attach the spreadsheet.
[04:20] Elena: trust center access  can auditors from our side get one-time access to your evidence and logs?
[04:26] Rohan: yes, we provide Trust Center with document artifacts (policies, certs, control evidence). For auditor access we can create auditor accounts with time-limited access or provide bundled artifacts including SOC 2 bridge letters and system descriptions. For live log access, that's possible via a read-only audit role combined with an export or temporary access token; we prefer exports to your storage for long-term retention.
[04:50] Priya: do you do penetration testing and share reports?
[04:53] Liam: we have a regular pentest cadence and we redact sensitive findings but share an executive summary and remediation status. We'll include pentest summary in the Trust Center artifacts.
[05:02] Elena: can you map specific SOC 2 CC controls to ISO 27001 controls  our auditor asked for crosswalk?
[05:08] Rohan: yes, our controls mapping spreadsheet crosswalks SOC 2 common criteria to ISO 27001 Annex A and includes sample evidence artifacts. We'll send that  it's the thing we mentioned earlier.
[05:18] David Park: for Dedicated, what's the network topology? Do you support VPC peering, private link, or customer-managed NAT?
[05:25] Rohan: Dedicated supports VPC peering and PrivateLink-type setups depending on cloud. You can configure private endpoints and route traffic through your VPC. For on-prem we provide an appliance/agent for network bridging. We'll include a topology diagram in the follow-up.
[05:40] Elena: one more  disclosure of sub-processors and suppliers  we need the list for our vendor risk management.
[05:45] Maya: we maintain a sub-processor list in Trust Center; it's regularly updated and includes cloud infra providers and logging vendors. We'll share the current document and include a summary of data flows.
[05:55] Priya: any certifications for your underlying cloud providers? Like ISO for the infra?
[05:58] Rohan: our cloud providers have their own ISO and SOC attestations, we reference those in the Trust Center.
[06:05] Elena: ok, sounds good. Timeline: we need artifacts by end of next week for our internal review. Can you meet that?
[06:10] Maya: yes  we can deliver SOC 2 Type II report, the controls mapping spreadsheet, Trust Center access steps, sample audit logs, and role matrix within 3 business days. Rohan will follow up with a Trust Center demo the following week.
[06:20] Carlos Ruiz: procurement question  do you support standard CSA or do you require our redlines?
[06:24] Maya: we have a standard master services agreement with a data processing addendum; we accept some redlines but have security and liability floors. Procurement can start review; we'll loop our legal team as needed.
[06:35] (brief cross-talk)
[06:40] Rohan: I'll also note that if you opt for Dedicated we'll include longer log retention and CMEK options baked into the contract which simplifies the procurement ask.
[06:50] Priya: one nit  you mentioned metadata replication in the DPA; can you specify which metadata is replicated and to where? That's important for our threat model.
[06:58] Liam: yes, that's a good point. The replicated metadata is control-plane metadata such as provisioning state, health checks, and anonymized usage metrics for billing. Customer content (prompts/responses) is not replicated outside the region unless you enable cross-region backups. We'll put exact fields in the tech appendix.
[07:15] Elena: ok great. any blockers from our side?
[07:18] Priya: just to confirm the log fields and sample payloads. We'll review the mapping spreadsheet and get back with specific control IDs we need mapped.
[07:25] Maya: perfect  recap of agreed next steps: I'll send SOC 2 Type II and DPA, controls mapping sheet, sub-processor list; Rohan will schedule a Trust Center demo and provide sample audit logs and role matrix; Priya will share the list of control IDs.
[07:40] Elena: thanks everyone. That should let us finish our vendor assessment.
[07:45] Maya: thanks all  we'll follow up by email and put the links in the CRM.

--- End of Call ---
